title: Frederick II's ciphered cabinet orders to his envoy Klinggraeffen at Dresden, 1744-56, 'mit Aufloesung in franzoesischer Sprache' (11 volumes)
correspondents: Frederick II -> Joachim Wilhelm von Klinggraeffen (Prussian envoy at Dresden); Nr. 781 also to Gotthard von Buelow, Leopold II of Anhalt-Dessau, F. A. von Rutowsky, and to the envoy J. E. von Wallenrodt (1744)
shelfmark: GStA PK, I. HA Rep. 81 (Gesandtschaft Dresden), Nr. 781-791
folio_note: Each volume: 'chiffrierte Kabinettsordern mit Aufloesung in franzoesischer Sprache' (Nr. 781 1744/46, 782 1747, 783 1748, 784 1748, 785 1749, 786 1750, 787 1750-51, 788 1752, 789 1753-54, 790 1755, 791 1756). Catalogue 593 mentions Nr. 782-784 only as a side note, not as a row. Nr. 792 (1752) holds drafts released for ciphering
status: Finding aid as quoted: every order is filed with its contemporary deciphered (French) form, so the plaintext of a whole run of Frederick II's cabinet ciphers is in the same volume. No decipherment published that this sweep found.
why: The largest paired cipher/plaintext set found in the Prussian foreign ministry's papers: eleven consecutive volumes of one king's orders to one envoy over twelve years, so a key can be rebuilt from pairs and checked across years (cipher changes show as breaks; the 1747 new cipher is in Rep. 41 Nr. 145). One key per correspondent, so the Anhalt-Dessau and Rutowsky pieces of Nr. 781 are separate sub-keys.
verify: Order Nr. 781 and 786 (two years apart); check whether the Aufloesung sits on the ciphered sheet; compare with catalogue 590 (Frederick II / Ulrike) and 593; look for Frederick's Dresden cipher in Rep. 41 Nr. 145 and the Rep. 81 Dresden key volumes.
